trigger: an audit-write failure on a read of a faulted device (REST 503 / MCP withheld body)
summary: record_section_integrity runs inside the one hw_ci_detail_fn closure, before the REST emit_behavioral_audit / MCP audit gate, so the counter and WARN move for a read whose body is then withheld; the text said 'served reads'. FIXED: wording is 'reads composed with a faulted section' in the describe text, metrics.md and the header; moving the call into the handlers would fork it across two transports.
classification_rationale: the docs and header claimed a count of served reads

trigger: an intermittent digest-provider failure between the body's verify call and the counter's second verify call
summary: The header claimed the counted cause is 'by construction' the served one, but the counter re-verifies the section (a second call), so a flapping provider could make the counted label differ from the served token (also unhappy-path UP-1, consistency C-2 for the structural variant). FIXED: ONE served_section_verdict called by both paths, and the header states the two-calls residual honestly; carrying a precomputed verdict was declined (it creates the second serving path the header forbids).
classification_rationale: a normative 'by construction' claim the code did not enforce

trigger: a status-only or unregistered kind that carries a stored row_count
summary: ci_sections_json verified only table-backed registered kinds while record_section_integrity verified every section in the vector, so the counter could count a fault the body does not carry (unreachable today). FIXED: both call served_section_verdict, which applies the registered/table-backed guard.
classification_rationale: the counter and the body used different predicates

trigger: the REST test 'only the REST record moves the section integrity counter; the dashboard never does'
summary: The fake ci_detail_fn re-implements the counting rule, so the test proves the route passes the right CiRead, not that the real closure counts only on WithSections; the 'Kills:' comments overclaimed. FIXED: comments say what the test proves; the real closure is pinned lexically (and the pin was tightened and mutation-checked).
classification_rationale: a test comment claimed more than the test establishes

trigger: an MCP call refused for an unrelated reason (argument shape, unwired dependency)
summary: The MCP half of the out-of-scope test asserted only contains("error") and checked ci_reads.empty() after BOTH transports, so it could pass vacuously. FIXED: asserts the error code and message, checks ci_reads.empty() after the MCP call and again after the REST call, the in-scope device is faulted and the test asserts ci_reads.size()==1 and the counter equals 1.
classification_rationale: a test that could not fail for the reason it was written for

trigger: someone deleting the pre-seed loop, adding a fault, or reordering the count/digest precedence
summary: No test that the three series exist at 0 (also consistency C-3: the pre-seed labels were a second hand-kept list), and gaps: count mismatch + failing provider, token joining after an agent reason, non-table kinds with a stored count, the quiet path. FIXED: register_section_integrity_metrics derives the labels from section_fault_label over kCountedFaults and a test asserts one series per counted fault at 0; the other cases were added.
classification_rationale: missing test coverage for behaviour the change introduced

trigger: a regression in how the unverifiable token reaches a REST or MCP body
summary: The new server:content_digest_unverifiable token is tested at verify_section_content and served_section_verdict level, not end-to-end through a REST or MCP body: hardware_ci_json and ci_sections_json take no digest provider, so reaching the branch through a transport needs a test-only parameter on the shared body builder (a production API change). NOT done by choice; the owner has been told.
classification_rationale: a test the change could carry but does not

trigger: a maintainer reading hardware_list_model as the pure model/serve layer
summary: A side-effecting sampler, metrics and logging lived in the 'pure model' TU. FIXED: moved to hardware_section_integrity.{hpp,cpp} (listed in server/core/meson.build); the model header is metrics-free again.
classification_rationale: layering against the header's own 'one serving path' separation

trigger: always
summary: A stray empty anonymous-namespace block left by the move (found independently by cpp-expert, cpp-safety, security-guardian and cross-platform). FIXED: removed.
classification_rationale: dead scaffolding, no behaviour

trigger: a future caller passing SectionFault::None to the sampler lookup
summary: SectionFault::None shared a case label with the unverifiable sampler (unreachable today because record_section_integrity returns early). FIXED: None has no sampler (the lookup returns nullptr).
classification_rationale: a latent mis-attribution

trigger: two threads racing the leading-edge exchange and the count increment
summary: exchange + fetch_add are two relaxed atomics, so one WARN can be missed or doubled. DECLINED: cosmetic, the same design as the existing DegradeSampler; the counter is the continuous signal and the WARN a sampled breadcrumb.
classification_rationale: accepted design, benign

trigger: production code calling the test-only digest provider setter
summary: DeviceInventoryStore::set_digest_provider_for_test is public with no compile-time guard. DECLINED: the repo has many such public *_for_test seams in production headers (engine_principal_store, enablement_store, credential_change_owner); a plain function pointer, no production caller (grep).
classification_rationale: accepted repo convention

trigger: an operator or maintainer reading the touched prose
summary: Four wording items (changelog tail contradicting the token change, alert-comment stutter, 'unverified' clashing with 'unverifiable', ambiguous 'it' in rest-api.md). FIXED.
classification_rationale: wording only

trigger: an operator reading ADR-0016's list of server: tokens
summary: ADR-0016 (lines ~1289/~1308) lists only the two mismatch tokens and omits server:content_digest_unverifiable. NOT edited here: another owner's item (#7042); flagged. To be filed or sent to that owner if the user asks.
classification_rationale: a doc obligation owned by someone else

trigger: an agentic worker reading the get_hardware_ci description for a server:content_digest_unverifiable section
summary: The MCP tool description said 'for any of these reasons do not retry the read, it will not change', which is true for the two mismatch tokens but not for unverifiable (recomputed per read; a transient provider fault can clear; persistent needs operator action on OpenSSL/FIPS; a device sync does not clear it). The reporter rated it SHOULD (I3); the recorder derives the consequence as a missed retry (degraded but correct). FIXED in the description, rest-api.md, mcp.md, inventory.md and the OpenAPI text.
classification_rationale: a machine-facing contract text contradicting the code

trigger: an auditor reading metrics.md or the MCP description in isolation
summary: The integrity counter's docs omitted that the digest detects accident and drift, not tampering (rest-api.md already says so); an isolated reader could take the counter as a tamper-evidence control. FIXED: the same sentence in the MCP description, mcp.md, inventory.md and metrics.md.
classification_rationale: a caveat required to avoid over-claiming a control

trigger: a source=device_ci sections_query_error rate above 0 for 5 minutes
summary: YuzuInventoryReadDegraded is reason-agnostic so it fires on the new reason, but no promtool case pinned it and the annotation named only the old reasons. FIXED: one annotation sentence (no expr/for/threshold change) and two promtool cases; the parent ran the repo's promtool runner (docker, pinned image): exit 0.
classification_rationale: an alert-rule edit with no test pinning that it fires

trigger: a non-zero digest_unverifiable rate
summary: 'Check OpenSSL/FIPS' was the whole instruction, and a fleet-wide burst had no next step. FIXED: concrete diagnostic (openssl list -providers in the server's environment and the startup log for provider/FIPS errors), the partial-restore step (re-run the restore or force a full device-record sync), and that the WARN is sampled and cannot list every device.
classification_rationale: a runbook step missing for a shipped signal

trigger: an operator who wants to be paged on served integrity faults
summary: No alert rule on yuzu_hardware_section_integrity_total (also unhappy-path UP-15, compliance). DEFERRED deliberately: thresholds are claims about fleet behaviour and belong in their own change tuned on real data; architect and sre both recommend FILING the follow-up rather than leaving it a note. Not filed without the user's ask.
classification_rationale: a signal with no consumer, by decision

trigger: a partial pg_restore faulting many devices at once
summary: The WARN is per reason (leading edge of a 60 s episode, then every 100th), so it cannot list the affected devices and an episode never ends under continuous polling. FIXED in the docs (sampled; read the responses or run a full sync); the sampler design is unchanged.
classification_rationale: operator expectation vs sampled logging

trigger: an edit that drops or inverts the ci_sections guard, passes nullptr for &metrics_, or wraps the call in if(false)
summary: The first pin left the guard, the &metrics_ argument and dead-branch variants unpinned. FIXED: the guard + call text, a single &metrics_, no nullptr/if(false)/#if 0/#ifdef in the closure body and the boot registration call are pinned; mutation-checked on a scratch copy: 14/14 killed, the two reformat mutants stay green.
classification_rationale: a regression net with holes

trigger: any WithSections read of a v2 record
summary: Each section is hashed twice per read (counter and body). DECLINED: bounded by the 96 KiB blob cap (tens of microseconds), dwarfed by the REPEATABLE READ transaction; sharing a precomputed verdict would create a second serving path.
classification_rationale: accepted cost

trigger: bad_alloc inside record_section_integrity
summary: A monitoring side effect inside the closure could fail a read that would otherwise succeed. DECLINED: the path allocates only a label string and logs, no worse than any other allocation on the request, and the closure has no other catch.
classification_rationale: accepted design

trigger: a fifth SectionFault enumerator added later
summary: kCountedFaults is hand-listed against the enum with no static_assert (cpp-expert, architect, consistency-auditor, unhappy-path, quality-engineer); its comment also said the sampler lookup iterates it though it is a switch. FIXED: a static_assert tying its size to the highest enumerator (a NEW trailing enumerator is caught by -Wswitch on the two switches) and a corrected comment.
classification_rationale: a comment contradicting the code plus a missing guard

trigger: a maintainer or operator conflating 'unverified' (digest not compared) with the new 'unverifiable' token
summary: Code comments still called a not-compared digest 'unverified'. FIXED to 'unchecked' / 'not compared' in six comments; inventory.md 'each served fault' became 'each faulted section of a read composed' and two over-long lines were re-wrapped.
classification_rationale: wording only

trigger: a reader of the test comment, the alert annotation or the verdict header
summary: Leftover 'served reads' in a test comment; the alert annotation said 'the record route answered 503' though the MCP tool returns a retryable error; the pre-seed test comment overclaimed that it catches label-list drift. FIXED.
classification_rationale: wording only

trigger: a future caller calling verify_section_content directly on a status-only kind with a stored count
summary: The header said anything serving raw levels must 'call one of the two', which is permissive: verify_section_content alone can report a fault the body never carries for such a kind. FIXED: serving paths MUST go through served_section_verdict.
classification_rationale: a comment inviting a divergent predicate
